Sour foods.Lemon: Lemon juice is about 5 to 6 percent citric acid, which is why it can 'cook' fish in ceviche by changing its proteins.
Sour foods.Lime: Limes are a bit more acidic than lemons. British sailors were nicknamed 'limeys' for the fruit they carried to prevent scurvy.
Sour foods.Sauerkraut: Sauerkraut is cabbage fermented with salt. Its sour tang comes from lactic acid bacteria, the same family as in yogurt.
Sour foods.Pickles: A cucumber becomes a pickle by soaking in vinegar or by lactic fermentation. Either way, acid makes it tangy.
Sour foods.Vinegar: The word comes from French 'vin aigre', meaning sour wine. Household vinegar is typically about 5 percent acetic acid.
Sour foods.Kimchi: Korea's fermented cabbage has hundreds of varieties. Its sourness grows as bacteria turn sugars into lactic acid over time.
Sour foods.Tamarind: A pod fruit with a sticky, sweet-sour pulp. It's a key flavor in Worcestershire sauce and many Indian and Thai dishes.
Sour foods.Rhubarb: Only the stalks are eaten; the leaves contain oxalic acid and are poisonous. Stalks are sour enough that nearly everyone sweetens them.
Sour foods.Sour Patch Kids: The candy is sour first, then sweet. The sour coating is acid crystals, and the sweet center shows up after it dissolves.
Sour foods.Granny Smith: The green apple is named for Maria Ann Smith, who grew the first tree in Australia in the 1860s. Its tartness comes from malic acid.
Sour foods.Cranberry: Cranberries are very tart and low in sugar, which is why juice and sauce are usually sweetened. Good ones bounce when ripe.
Sour foods.Honey: Honey is sweet, but it's also quite acidic, with a pH around 4. Sugar masks the acid, so your tongue reads sweet.
Sour foods.Banana: Banana is sweet and low in acid. Its sugar content rises as it ripens, as the starch converts.
Sour foods.Milk chocolate: Sweet and creamy, with sugar and milk covering the cocoa's natural bitterness and acidity.
Sour foods.Bread: Plain bread is mild. But sourdough is a trap of sorts, as its tang comes from acids made by wild yeast and bacteria.
Sour foods.Potato: Potatoes taste mild and starchy, with no real sourness.
Sour foods.Rice: Plain rice is mild and subtly sweet. Its starch breaks into sugars on the tongue as you chew.
Sour foods.Cucumber: Cucumbers are mild and watery. They become sour only after pickling in vinegar or brine.
Sour foods.Watermelon: About 92 percent water with sweet flesh. A ripe one has a creamy yellow spot where it rested on the ground.
Sour foods.Marshmallow: Sweet, soft and almost pure sugar, with no acid. It gets its fluff from air whipped into a gelatin syrup.
Sour foods.Butter: Butter is rich and creamy, though cultured butter is fermented and can have a slight tang.
Sour foods.Caramel: Caramel is heated sugar, giving sweet and a little bitter flavor, but it's not sour.
Sour foods.Cotton candy: Pure spun sugar, so intensely sweet. It's mostly air, and a big cloud holds the sugar of a small candy.
Sour foods.Sweet potato: Sweet potatoes are sweet, and baking converts more starch to sugar. Despite the name, they're not related to ordinary potatoes.

Animals that can outrun Usain Bolt.Pronghorn: North America's fastest land animal, with bursts around 85 km/h and the stamina to run for long distances.
Animals that can outrun Usain Bolt.Horse: A galloping horse reaches about 50 to 70 km/h, far more than Bolt's top speed of roughly 44 km/h.
Animals that can outrun Usain Bolt.Greyhound: The fastest dog, hitting about 65 to 70 km/h, easily outpacing Bolt.
Animals that can outrun Usain Bolt.Ostrich: The fastest bird on land, sprinting at about 70 km/h, and can keep a steady pace for a long time.
Animals that can outrun Usain Bolt.Lion: A lion can sprint at about 55 to 80 km/h in short bursts, faster than Usain Bolt.
Animals that can outrun Usain Bolt.Gazelle: Thomson's gazelles reach about 80 km/h, and bounce while running in a movement called stotting.
Animals that can outrun Usain Bolt.Kangaroo: A red kangaroo can hop at around 60 km/h for short stretches, much faster than a human sprinter.
Animals that can outrun Usain Bolt.Zebra: A zebra can gallop at around 65 km/h, enough to outrun many predators and Bolt.
Animals that can outrun Usain Bolt.Hare: A hare can run about 70 km/h and zigzags to throw off pursuers. Unlike rabbits, hares are born furred with eyes open.
Animals that can outrun Usain Bolt.Wildebeest: A wildebeest can run about 80 km/h, helping it escape lions during its long migration across the Serengeti.
Animals that can outrun Usain Bolt.Coyote: A coyote can run about 65 km/h, faster than Bolt, and is a clever survivor across North America.
Animals that can outrun Usain Bolt.Tortoise: Tortoises plod at well under 1 km/h, so Bolt would win easily. In the fable, the tortoise only beat a sleeping hare.
Animals that can outrun Usain Bolt.Sloth: A sloth moves at about 0.2 km/h on the ground. It descends from its tree around once a week.
Animals that can outrun Usain Bolt.Snail: A garden snail moves at about 0.05 km/h, thousands of times slower than Bolt.
Animals that can outrun Usain Bolt.Koala: Koalas can scamper up a trunk surprisingly fast when startled, but they sleep most of the day. On the ground, Bolt would win easily.
Animals that can outrun Usain Bolt.Penguin: On land, penguins waddle at only a few km/h, but they swim much faster, up to 35 km/h in some species.
Animals that can outrun Usain Bolt.Hedgehog: A hedgehog runs about 6 to 8 km/h, far slower than Bolt, and prefers to curl up into a ball.
Animals that can outrun Usain Bolt.Chicken: Chickens can run about 14 km/h, far slower than Bolt's 44 km/h, though they can flutter short distances.
Animals that can outrun Usain Bolt.Turtle: A land turtle moves at well under 1 km/h, so Bolt would win easily. Sea turtles are quicker, but only in water.
Animals that can outrun Usain Bolt.Hippo: A hippo can run about 30 km/h on land over short distances, so Bolt's 44 km/h peak beats it, but only barely.
Animals that can outrun Usain Bolt.Panda: A giant panda can run about 30 km/h in an emergency, but it prefers a slow pace, and Bolt would win.
Animals that can outrun Usain Bolt.Pig: A pig can run at around 17 km/h, so Bolt would beat it. Pigs are also clever: they can learn to use a mirror to find hidden food.
Animals that can outrun Usain Bolt.Crocodile: A crocodile sprints at about 15 km/h on land, so Bolt is faster, though not in water.

Volcanoes.Vesuvius: Its AD 79 eruption buried Pompeii and Herculaneum under ash; it is still active and one of the world's most dangerous volcanoes.
Volcanoes.Etna: Europe's tallest and busiest volcano on Sicily erupts so often that its height changes. It has been active for about half a million years.
Volcanoes.Krakatoa: Its 1883 eruption was heard thousands of kilometers away, and the resulting tsunamis killed tens of thousands in Indonesia.
Volcanoes.Mount St. Helens: The 1980 eruption in Washington State was the deadliest in US history; it blew off the top of the mountain, lowering it by about 400 meters.
Volcanoes.Kilimanjaro: Africa's highest peak is a dormant volcano, and its snowy cap is shrinking quickly. It stands about 5,895 meters high.
Volcanoes.Mount Fuji: Japan's iconic peak is an active volcano that last erupted in 1707. It is climbed by hundreds of thousands each summer.
Volcanoes.Mauna Loa: Hawaii's giant shield volcano is Earth's largest active volcano by volume, and it erupted most recently in 2022.
Volcanoes.Kilauea: A Hawaiian volcano that has erupted nearly nonstop for decades; in 2018 it destroyed hundreds of homes.
Volcanoes.Pinatubo: In 1991 this Philippine volcano exploded in one of the century's largest eruptions, and its ash cooled the whole planet by about half a degree.
Volcanoes.Stromboli: An Italian island volcano that has erupted almost continuously for around two thousand years, earning the nickname Lighthouse of the Mediterranean.
Volcanoes.Mount Rainier: Washington's tallest peak is an active volcano capped with more glacial ice than any other mountain in the lower 48 states.
Volcanoes.Mount Hood: Oregon's highest peak is a volcano that is considered potentially active, though its last major eruptions came in the 1800s.
Volcanoes.Everest: Earth's highest mountain at about 8,849 meters, but it was formed by colliding plates, not by a volcano.
Volcanoes.K2: The world's second-highest peak is a non-volcanic mountain, and it is notoriously harder and deadlier to climb than Everest.
Volcanoes.Matterhorn: This Alpine pyramid is a fold of ancient rock thrust up by colliding continents, not a volcano.
Volcanoes.Mont Blanc: The Alps' highest peak is formed from granite and uplift, not volcanic activity.
Volcanoes.Denali: North America's tallest peak is a granite mountain uplifted by plate collision, not a volcano.
Volcanoes.Ben Nevis: Britain's highest peak is the eroded core of a volcano that collapsed about 400 million years ago, so it is long extinct.
Volcanoes.Mount Rushmore: Carved granite, not a volcano: the four presidents' faces are each about 18 meters tall.
Volcanoes.Table Mountain: Cape Town's flat-topped landmark is made of sandstone, not a volcano, and often wears a cloud called the tablecloth.
Volcanoes.Uluru: Australia's giant red monolith is sandstone, not volcanic, and most of it lies hidden underground.
Volcanoes.Annapurna: A Himalayan peak formed by plate collision, not volcanism; it is among the deadliest 8,000-meter mountains to climb.
Volcanoes.Half Dome: Yosemite's granite landmark was shaped by glaciers and erosion, not volcanic action.
Volcanoes.Kangchenjunga: The world's third-highest mountain is a non-volcanic Himalayan giant on the Nepal-India border.

Italian wines.Chianti: Tuscany's famous red, made mainly from Sangiovese and marked with a black rooster. It was once sold in straw-covered fiasco bottles.
Italian wines.Barolo: Piedmont's 'king of wines', made from Nebbiolo and aged for years before release. Its tannins are intense, and its tar-and-roses aroma is famous.
Italian wines.Prosecco: Italy's sparkling wine, made in the Veneto from Glera grapes. It gets its bubbles in tanks, not bottles, which keeps it fresh and cheaper than Champagne.
Italian wines.Brunello: A Tuscan red from Montalcino made from 100 percent Sangiovese grosso. It must age at least five years, and its name means little dark one.
Italian wines.Amarone: Veneto red made from partly dried grapes, which gives a rich, high-alcohol wine. Its name comes from amaro, 'bitter', in contrast to sweet Recioto.
Italian wines.Barbaresco: Piedmont's sibling of Barolo, from Nebbiolo grown near the village of Barbaresco, and usually a bit softer and ready earlier.
Italian wines.Lambrusco: A fizzy red from Emilia-Romagna, usually dry and good with rich local food such as mortadella and cured pork. Its name has nothing to do with the sweet export version of the 1970s.
Italian wines.Soave: A white from near Verona, based on Garganega, drunk young. It is among Italy's most exported wines, named after a village.
Italian wines.Valpolicella: A Veneto red, whose name means 'valley of many cellars' in Latin. It is a lighter cousin of Amarone, and uses the same grapes.
Italian wines.Franciacorta: Lombardy's answer to Champagne, a sparkling wine made by the traditional method with bottle fermentation, from Chardonnay and Pinot grapes.
Italian wines.Nero d'Avola: Sicily's signature red grape, whose name means 'black of Avola'. It grows in the southeast of the island and gives juicy, sun-ripe wines.
Italian wines.Moscato d'Asti: A lightly sparkling, sweet white from Piedmont. It has only around 5 percent alcohol, so it makes a perfect dessert wine.
Italian wines.Rioja: A trap: it's Spain's famous red region, in the north. It is Spanish and aged in oak, not Italian.
Italian wines.Cava: Spain's sparkling wine, mostly from Catalonia. It is made the same way as Champagne but is Spanish.
Italian wines.Bordeaux: Though some think Italian, this is a French region, whose Cabernet and Merlot blends are exported worldwide.
Italian wines.Beaujolais: A French red made from Gamay; its Nouveau is released in November each year. French, not Italian.
Italian wines.Champagne: France's famous sparkling wine. It's French, and only the wine from the Champagne region can use the name.
Italian wines.Port: Portugal's fortified wine from the Douro valley, aged in barrels and named for the port of Porto. Not Italian.
Italian wines.Tokaji: Hungary's sweet wine, whose name means 'from Tokaj'. It is made from grapes with noble rot. Hungarian.
Italian wines.Retsina: Greece's resin-flavoured wine, which was sealed with pine resin in ancient times. It is Greek and an acquired taste.
Italian wines.Sherry: A fortified wine from Jerez in Spain, in styles from bone-dry fino to sweet. Spanish, not Italian.
Italian wines.Chablis: A French white from Burgundy's northernmost region, made from Chardonnay, and almost always unoaked and mineral.
Italian wines.Madeira: A Portuguese island's wine, heated and oxidised on purpose, so it can last for centuries after opening.
Italian wines.Sancerre: A trap: it is a French white wine, made from Sauvignon Blanc in the Loire Valley, so it fits somewhere else but not in Italy.

Cities in Canada.Toronto: Toronto is Canada's biggest city, and one of the world's most multicultural, with over half its residents born abroad.
Cities in Canada.Montreal: Montreal is the second-largest French-speaking city in the world after Paris, by some counts, and it has an underground city.
Cities in Canada.Vancouver: Vancouver sits between mountains and the sea, so you could ski and sail on the same day.
Cities in Canada.Ottawa: Ottawa, not Toronto, is Canada's capital, chosen by Queen Victoria in 1857, and its canal becomes the world's largest skating rink.
Cities in Canada.Calgary: Calgary hosts the Stampede, a rodeo billed as the greatest outdoor show on Earth, and it held the 1988 Winter Olympics.
Cities in Canada.Edmonton: Edmonton is home to West Edmonton Mall, once the biggest mall in the world.
Cities in Canada.Winnipeg: Winnipeg gave its name to Winnie the bear, a Canadian army mascot who inspired A. A. Milne's Winnie-the-Pooh.
Cities in Canada.Quebec City: Quebec City is North America's only walled city north of Mexico, with a castle-like hotel, the Château Frontenac.
Cities in Canada.Halifax: Halifax is the Atlantic port where ships brought Titanic's victims, and many are buried in its cemeteries.
Cities in Canada.Regina: Regina is the capital of Saskatchewan, and it was originally called Pile o' Bones for the buffalo bones piled there.
Cities in Canada.Saskatoon: Saskatoon is named for a berry, and is known as the City of Bridges for its many river crossings.
Cities in Canada.Whitehorse: Whitehorse is the capital of the Yukon, and a good place to watch the northern lights.
Cities in Canada.Seattle: Seattle is in Washington State, in the US, and is home to Starbucks and the Space Needle.
Cities in Canada.Portland: Portland is in Oregon, and is known as the City of Roses.
Cities in Canada.Minneapolis: Minneapolis is in the US, and sits on the Mississippi, near the Minnesota lakes.
Cities in Canada.Detroit: Detroit is in Michigan, and is one of the few US cities where Canada lies to the south, across the river at Windsor.
Cities in Canada.Buffalo: Buffalo is in New York, and is close to Niagara Falls on the Canadian border.
Cities in Canada.Anchorage: Anchorage is Alaska's largest city, and in the US, not Canada.
Cities in Canada.Boston: Boston is in Massachusetts, and its Freedom Trail links historic American Revolution sites.
Cities in Canada.Chicago: Chicago is in Illinois, and it's the home of the first skyscraper.
Cities in Canada.Spokane: Spokane is in Washington State, near the Idaho border and some way south of Canada.
Cities in Canada.Fargo: Fargo is in North Dakota, and gave its name to a film and TV series that has little to do with the city.
Cities in Canada.Juneau: Juneau is the capital of Alaska, and reachable only by sea or air, as no road connects it to the rest of the state.
Cities in Canada.Cleveland: Cleveland is in Ohio, and is home to the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.

Currencies of Europe past or present.Euro: Introduced as cash in 2002, it is now used by over 20 countries, and it replaced currencies like the franc, mark and lira.
Currencies of Europe past or present.Pound: Sterling is the oldest currency still in use, with roots going back more than a thousand years, and the pound sign comes from the Latin libra.
Currencies of Europe past or present.Krona: Sweden's currency and Iceland's króna share a name meaning crown, and Sweden still uses it instead of the euro.
Currencies of Europe past or present.Krone: Norway and Denmark both use the krone, whose name means crown, and neither has joined the euro.
Currencies of Europe past or present.Zloty: Poland's currency, whose name means golden, has been reborn several times, and Poland still has not adopted the euro.
Currencies of Europe past or present.Forint: Hungary's currency, named after the Florence gold florin, was launched in 1946 after the worst hyperinflation in history.
Currencies of Europe past or present.Drachma: One of the oldest currencies in the world, used in ancient Greece and replaced by the euro in 2002.
Currencies of Europe past or present.Peseta: Spain's currency until 2002, its name is the diminutive of peso, meaning a little weight.
Currencies of Europe past or present.Deutsche Mark: Germany's currency after 1948 became a symbol of postwar recovery, and it was retired in 2002.
Currencies of Europe past or present.Escudo: Portugal's old currency before the euro, whose name means shield.
Currencies of Europe past or present.Guilder: The Dutch currency was called the gulden, and it was replaced by the euro in 2002.
Currencies of Europe past or present.Lev: Bulgaria's currency, whose name means lion, was due to give way to the euro in January 2026.
Currencies of Europe past or present.Lira: Italy's currency before the euro, and Turkey still uses a lira, so it can be called European in part.
Currencies of Europe past or present.Yen: Japan's currency, which is the third most traded in the world, and Japan is not in Europe.
Currencies of Europe past or present.Yuan: China's currency, also called the renminbi, which means the people's money.
Currencies of Europe past or present.Rupee: Used in India, Pakistan, Sri Lanka and Nepal, and its name comes from a Sanskrit word for silver.
Currencies of Europe past or present.Rand: South Africa's currency is named after the Witwatersrand, the gold-rich ridge near Johannesburg.
Currencies of Europe past or present.Baht: Thailand's currency, whose name comes from an old unit of weight.
Currencies of Europe past or present.Won: The currency of South and North Korea, and its name is related to the word round.
Currencies of Europe past or present.Dirham: Used in the UAE and Morocco, its name comes from the Greek drachma.
Currencies of Europe past or present.Riyal: The currency of Saudi Arabia, Qatar and others, and its name comes from the Spanish real.
Currencies of Europe past or present.Naira: Nigeria's currency, which was introduced in 1973 when the country replaced the pound.
Currencies of Europe past or present.Shekel: Israel's currency, taking its name from an ancient unit of weight mentioned in the Bible.
Currencies of Europe past or present.Kwacha: Used in Zambia and Malawi, the word means dawn in local languages.

Highest peak in its country.Kilimanjaro: Africa's highest peak at 5,895 meters, in Tanzania, is a freestanding volcano whose glaciers have been shrinking rapidly.

Highest peak in its country.Ben Nevis: The highest mountain in Britain, at 1,345 meters, has a summit with cloud cover for most of the year.
Highest peak in its country.Zugspitze: Germany's top at 2,962 meters, on the Austrian border, has a cable car and a glacier ski area.
Highest peak in its country.Mount Olympus: Greece's highest mountain, about 2,917 meters, was the home of the gods in ancient myth.
Highest peak in its country.Mount Fuji: Japan's highest peak, at 3,776 meters, is an active volcano that last erupted in 1707.
Highest peak in its country.Mount Elbrus: At 5,642 meters in the Caucasus, it is Europe's highest peak by one common definition, and Russia's tallest.
Highest peak in its country.Mount Logan: Canada's highest peak, about 5,959 meters, is in Yukon and is massive enough to have the largest base of any non-volcanic mountain on Earth.
Highest peak in its country.Mount Teide: The Canary Islands volcano on Tenerife is Spain's highest peak, about 3,715 meters, and its shadow reaches the sea.
Highest peak in its country.Grossglockner: Austria's highest peak, about 3,798 meters, is reached by a famous high alpine road.
Highest peak in its country.Mount Kenya: The country's highest peak, at about 5,200 meters, sits near the equator yet has glaciers.
Highest peak in its country.Matterhorn: This iconic pyramid on the Swiss-Italian border is not the highest in either country; Monte Rosa is higher in Switzerland.
Highest peak in its country.Mount Rainier: Washington's volcano, about 4,392 meters, is high but not the highest in the US; Denali is.
Highest peak in its country.Mount Whitney: At 4,421 meters it is the tallest in the lower 48 states, but not in the whole US, as Denali is taller.
Highest peak in its country.Mount Washington: The top of New Hampshire's White Mountains is famous for extreme weather, but it isn't the nation's highest.
Highest peak in its country.Eiger: Famous for its north face in the Swiss Alps, but Switzerland's highest peak is Dufourspitze.
Highest peak in its country.Mount Etna: Europe's most active volcano in Sicily, around 3,300 meters, is Italy's tallest volcano but far lower than the Alps.
Highest peak in its country.Vesuvius: The volcano that buried Pompeii in 79 AD stands over Naples, and it is not Italy's highest mountain.
Highest peak in its country.Table Mountain: The flat-topped peak above Cape Town is a landmark, but not South Africa's highest.
Highest peak in its country.Mount Hood: Oregon's tallest peak, at about 3,429 meters, is not the highest in the United States.
Highest peak in its country.Ben Lomond: A Scottish peak by the loch that is popular with walkers, though Ben Nevis is the highest.
Highest peak in its country.Jungfrau: A 4,158 meter peak in the Swiss Alps with Europe's highest railway station, but not Switzerland's highest.

Songs from Disney animated films.How Far I'll Go: Lin-Manuel Miranda wrote Moana's anthem, and Auli'i Cravalho sang it, earning an Oscar nomination.
Songs from Disney animated films.You're Welcome: Lin-Manuel Miranda wrote Maui's brag song, and Dwayne Johnson, who is of Samoan heritage, sings it.
Songs from Disney animated films.Part of Your World: Ariel's 'I want' song nearly got cut from The Little Mermaid after a test screening where kids seemed to lose interest.
Songs from Disney animated films.Colors of the Wind: Pocahontas's ballad won the Oscar for Best Original Song, written by Alan Menken and Stephen Schwartz.

Songs from Disney animated films.Happy: Pharrell's 'Happy' came from Despicable Me 2, an Illumination film, and it was Oscar-nominated.
Songs from Disney animated films.I Like to Move It: This 1993 Reel 2 Real dance hit became King Julien's anthem in DreamWorks' Madagascar.
Songs from Disney animated films.Hallelujah: Leonard Cohen's song plays in Shrek in a John Cale version, so it isn't from a Disney animation.
Songs from Disney animated films.My Heart Will Go On: Celine Dion's song is from Titanic (1997), not a Disney animated film, with music by James Horner.
Songs from Disney animated films.Somewhere Out There: Linda Ronstadt and James Ingram sang this song for Universal and Amblin's An American Tail in 1986.
Songs from Disney animated films.Over the Rainbow: The Wizard of Oz song won the 1939 Oscar, but that was MGM, not Disney.
Songs from Disney animated films.Peaches: Jack Black's Bowser sings 'Peaches' in The Super Mario Bros. Movie, from Illumination, not Disney.
Songs from Disney animated films.Eye of the Tiger: Survivor's anthem comes from Rocky III in 1982, with no connection to Disney animation.
Songs from Disney animated films.Accidentally in Love: Counting Crows' song from Shrek 2 earned an Oscar nomination, but it's DreamWorks, not Disney.
